_: Need for Speed's track geometry is already metres — the disc stores 16.16
fixed point and nfs.Float divides by 65536, road segments 6 m apart — so
metresPerUnit is 1 and there is nothing to derive.
The spawn is the exported grid camera (webexport/main.go startCamera, itself
calibrated against the running game's camObj to 4 mm) with the driver's eye
height taken back off: segment 16, 96 m in, 2.9 m right of the centreline,
The two cars sit where a race starts, a lane either side of you.
_spawn: On the centre line, 8 m behind the grid, so both cars are ahead of you.
The calibrated grid camera is at [-2.902, 0.94, -96] — segment 16, 2.9 m
right of the centreline, driver's eye height — but that is where the
PLAYER'S OWN CAR is, so standing there puts you inside the Ferrari.
_sky: sky-cy1.glb is a UNIT-RADIUS cylinder, camera-attached. On a monitor that
is invisible; in stereo it is a horizon one metre from your face, with
about 6.4% parallax between the eyes. scale:auto pushes it to 0.45 of the
far plane, where the parallax is 0.011%. fog:false because a horizon that
fogs out is not a horizon — the terrain is what blends into it.
_props: The two lanes, measured off the geometry rather than off the docs. Probing
the cross-section at z = -96 gives the carriageway as material 0 spanning
x -5.00 .. +5.00 — two 5 m lanes with the centre line at 0 — flanked by
shoulders out to -15.25 and +11.00 and then embankments. The docs' 'eight
lanes of 5 m spanning +-20' is the road model, not this segment: at -7.5
the Ferrari was standing on the hard strip.
+-2.5 is also where the game's own traced grid puts the two cars.
rotY 0 = the model's own -Z, the direction the course runs. Both models are
4.4-4.6 long on Z and sit on y = 0, so they need no height offset.
